messages:
jamal: FYI — after landing the rbac-refactor today, a customer (org: acme-ops) reports they can list audit logs for a different project. Not good. /cc @maria @lina

maria: steps to reproduce?

jamal: steps:
1) as user from org acme-ops, call GET /v1/audit/logs?workspace=proj-b
2) response 200 with logs for proj-b
Log excerpt:
```
time=2026-03-20T15:12:03Z user=alice@acme-ops action=read_logs workspace=proj-b requester_org=acme-ops policy_evaluated=ALLOW source=rbac-service
```
We expect policy_evaluated=DENY.

sec-bot: Alert created: rbac-incident-1779991110, severity=high

lina: can you paste the PR that landed? I suspect alias->org mapping bug.

jamal: PR https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/2045 — lines changed in rbac/mapper.go:
```
if alias == '' {
  return orgID // <- bug: should return empty and fallthrough to deny
}
```
rolling back now.

ops-sre: rolling back infra deployment to previous tag infra@v1.12.3, estimating 3 mins

deploy-bot: rollback started by ops-sre for infra cluster prod-eu, job id 6421

jamal: rollback completed, tests show access now denied. I opened an internal postmortem ticket: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/SEC-2413. We'll push a proper fix that inverts the conditional and add unit tests + integration test for cross-org access.

maria: thanks. please add audit log sampling to verify no other workspaces affected. @sec-bot can you run a quick scan across orgs for any ALLOW where requester_org != workspace_owner_org in last 24h?

sec-bot: scan queued. initial results: 2 suspicious hits in staging, none in prod beyond the reported one. will post full results in thread.

lina: good. we should schedule a quick post-incident review with infra + sec + sres tomorrow. :calendar:
